method_card.title: Solving Inequalities
method_card.content:
Inequalities use \(<\), \(>\), \(\leq\), \(\geq\) instead of \(=\). Solve them exactly like equations, with one rule: if you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the sign, so \(<\) becomes \(>\).

A strict symbol (\(<\), \(>\)) does not include the boundary; \(\leq\) and \(\geq\) do. For a double inequality like \(2 < x + 1 \leq 5\), do the same step to all three parts: \(1 < x \leq 4\).
method_card.example:
Solve \(3x + 5 > 14\)

Subtract 5: \(3x > 9\). Divide by 3: \(x > 3\). The answer is every number greater than 3.
